<div class="learn-box">
**What you will learn**

Bind measurements at a common date, derive BMI, mean arterial pressure and a
ratio, and check the inputs needed for eGFR and duplicate handling.
</div>

**You need:** the packages, downloaded helpers and two loaded resources in
[Before you start](book-00-start.html#before-you-start), plus the recipe basics
from [chapter 6](book-06-events.html). Start a fresh R session in `book-work`.
Run the sections in order: each uses objects defined immediately above it.

This chapter uses **synthetic Synthea27Nj measurements**, described in
[Getting started](book-00-start.html#load-two-public-synthetic-datasets).

Concept selections refer to the searches and saved definitions in
[chapter 4](book-04-vocabulary.html), including the separate questionnaire
catalogue. Additional body-measurement concepts are found on screen in the
[formula walkthrough](book-15-formulas.html#find-the-inputs-before-calculating).

## Find the inputs before calculating

Use the same Synthea resource as the lab chapter. A formula does not make inputs
comparable: check the measurement meaning, units and date before combining them.


``` r
library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
source("tools/book/case-helpers.R")
practice <- book_connect("numeric")
conns <- practice$conns
```

Search weight and height separately. The search rows carry standard status,
concept class and validity dates. Select an exact name, not the first search hit.


``` r
weight_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Body weight", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
height_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Body height", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(rbind(weight_hits, height_hits)[c("concept_name", "standard_concept", "vocabulary_id")])
```



|concept_name |standard_concept |vocabulary_id |
|:------------|:----------------|:-------------|
|Body weight  |S                |LOINC         |
|Body height  |S                |LOINC         |

``` r
weight_id <- weight_hits$concept_id[trimws(weight_hits$concept_name) == "Body weight"]
height_id <- height_hits$concept_id[trimws(height_hits$concept_name) == "Body height"]
body_sets <- list(weight = omop_concept_set(weight_id), height = omop_concept_set(height_id))
```


``` r
weight_units <- ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = weight_id,
  scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled
height_units <- ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = height_id,
  scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(weight_units)
```



|   n|concept_name |value |
|---:|:------------|:-----|
| 510|kilogram     |9529  |

``` r
knitr::kable(height_units)
```



|   n|concept_name |value |
|---:|:------------|:-----|
| 495|centimeter   |8582  |

The unit IDs used below were returned by those protected inventories. In the
practice source they mean kilogram and centimetre, as also inspected in chapter 4.

## Bind weight and height on the same day

Index on first weight. The exact-day tolerance selects both inputs at that date.
An absent height stays missing; choosing a distant height silently would change
the formula's meaning. Synthea includes children, so do not apply adult BMI bands.


``` r
weight_event <- omop_event("measurement", body_sets$weight)
weight <- omop_value_at_index("measurement", body_sets$weight, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = omop_unit(9529L))
height <- omop_value_at_index("measurement", body_sets$height, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = omop_unit(8582L))
```

## Declare a named BMI formula

The formula requires kilograms and metres. Declare the conversion from each
recorded unit into its physical coordinate. A factor of 0.01 converts centimetres
to metres; it is not a display-only rename.


``` r
weight_kg <- omop_number(weight, omop_number_spec(unit =
  omop_number_unit("unit:9529", "coordinate:kg", factor = 1)))
height_m <- omop_number(height, omop_number_spec(unit =
  omop_number_unit("unit:8582", "coordinate:metres", factor = 0.01)))
bmi <- omop_formula_bmi(weight_kg, height_m)
body <- omop_study(weight_event, outputs = "baseline",
  baseline = list(weight = weight, height = height, bmi = bmi))
body_result <- recipe_execute(body, out = c(baseline = "D_formula_body"), conns = conns)
knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_formula_body$bmi", datasources = conns)))
```



|Site |Statistic |    Value|
|:----|:---------|--------:|
|site |5%        | 11.53374|
|site |10%       | 13.62216|
|site |25%       | 15.88957|
|site |50%       | 23.86380|
|site |75%       | 27.93787|
|site |90%       | 30.20849|
|site |95%       | 30.36386|
|site |Mean      | 22.11315|

BMI is kg divided by metres squared. The helper uses the presented coordinates,
requires positive finite inputs and records its equation and definition version
in the codebook. Missing or invalid inputs become missing privately. Same-day
alignment remains a study decision; a formula does not create it automatically.

**Exercise 1.** Round BMI to one decimal for presentation while keeping the
unrounded formula available.

<details><summary>Solution 1</summary>


``` r
body_rounded <- omop_study(weight_event, outputs = "baseline",
  baseline = list(bmi = bmi, rounded = omop_number(bmi,
    omop_number_spec(rounding = omop_number_round("decimals", 1)))))
book_symbols(recipe_execute(body_rounded, out = c(baseline = "D_formula_rounded"), conns = conns))
```

## Mean arterial pressure and a ratio

Find systolic and diastolic pressure, inspect their recorded units, then bind both
to the same systolic measurement date. The familiar approximate MAP formula is
(SBP + 2 × DBP) / 3; it is a derived estimate, not a separately measured pressure.


``` r
sbp_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Systolic blood pressure", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
dbp_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Diastolic blood pressure", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(rbind(sbp_hits, dbp_hits)[c("concept_name", "standard_concept", "vocabulary_id")])
```



|concept_name                          |standard_concept |vocabulary_id |
|:-------------------------------------|:----------------|:-------------|
|Blood pressure systolic and diastolic |S                |LOINC         |
|Systolic blood pressure               |S                |LOINC         |
|Blood pressure systolic and diastolic |S                |LOINC         |
|Diastolic blood pressure              |S                |LOINC         |

``` r
sbp_id <- sbp_hits$concept_id[trimws(sbp_hits$concept_name) == "Systolic blood pressure"]
dbp_id <- dbp_hits$concept_id[trimws(dbp_hits$concept_name) == "Diastolic blood pressure"]
knitr::kable(ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = sbp_id,
  scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled)
```



|   n|concept_name              |value |
|---:|:-------------------------|:-----|
| 725|millimeter mercury column |8876  |


``` r
sbp_event <- omop_event("measurement", omop_concept_set(sbp_id))
sbp <- omop_value_at_index("measurement", sbp_id, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = omop_unit(8876L))
dbp <- omop_value_at_index("measurement", dbp_id, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = omop_unit(8876L))
sbp_mmhg <- omop_number(sbp, omop_number_spec(unit =
  omop_number_unit("unit:8876", "coordinate:mmHg", factor = 1)))
dbp_mmhg <- omop_number(dbp, omop_number_spec(unit =
  omop_number_unit("unit:8876", "coordinate:mmHg", factor = 1)))
map <- omop_formula_map(sbp_mmhg, dbp_mmhg)
ratio <- omop_formula_ratio(sbp_mmhg, dbp_mmhg, unit = "1")
pressure <- omop_study(sbp_event, outputs = "baseline", baseline = list(map = map, ratio = ratio))
book_symbols(recipe_execute(pressure, out = c(baseline = "D_formula_pressure"), conns = conns))
```


## eGFR: validate the prerequisites before deriving

The race-free adult CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine equation needs serum creatinine,
age and sex. Its public formula is
142 × min(Scr/κ, 1)^α × max(Scr/κ, 1)^−1.2 × 0.9938^age,
with κ = 0.7 and α = −0.241 for female, κ = 0.9 and α = −0.302
for male, and a further factor 1.012 for female. Scr is in mg/dL.
See the [National Kidney Foundation equation](https://www.kidney.org/ckd-epi-creatinine-equation-2021).

Do not substitute a different specimen because the correct source is sparse.
This check distinguishes vocabulary availability from observed use:

<!-- expected-refusal:start -->

``` r
creatinine_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Creatinine", domain = "Measurement",
  vocabulary = "LOINC", conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(creatinine_hits[c("concept_name", "standard_concept")])
```



|concept_name                                  |standard_concept |
|:---------------------------------------------|:----------------|
|Microalbumin/Creatinine [Mass Ratio] in Urine |S                |
|Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma   |S                |
|Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Blood             |S                |

``` r
serum_id <- creatinine_hits$concept_id[trimws(creatinine_hits$concept_name) ==
  "Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma"]
serum_set <- omop_concept_set(serum_id)
serum_locations <- ds.omop.concept.locate(serum_id, scope = "pooled", conns = conns)
serum_locations
```

```
#> <dsomop_result>
#> Servers: site
#> Scope: pooled
#> 
#> $site
#> [1] table_name     concept_column concept_id     n_records      n_persons     
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
#> 
#> Warnings:
#>   - Strict pooling failed: invalid concept locator from server site
#>   - No complete disclosure-safe pooled concept-location result was available.
```

<!-- expected-refusal:end -->

The catalogue contains both Blood and Serum or Plasma creatinine. The locator
returns an empty site result and reports that strict pooling failed; there is no
admitted pooled source-use result. This is inconclusive about suitable serum
measurements, not evidence of their absence or a reason to substitute Blood.
This lesson therefore does not report patient eGFR.
The named helper `omop_formula_egfr_ckdepi2021()` requires standardized creatinine
in `coordinate:idms_creatinine_mg_dl`, completed calendar age at that same
measurement, and an explicit public mapping from the study's sex categories to
the equation branches. A field named gender does not establish that mapping.
The formula returns missing for children, nonpositive creatinine and unmapped sex.

The source check above is a reason to stop this Synthea calculation: neither
renaming Blood as Serum nor declaring an assay coordinate establishes specimen
or assay suitability. The worked formula below uses a separate synthetic teaching example with known
input meaning. It does not reinterpret the Synthea records.

**Exercise 3.** Why would using the first creatinine search hit be unsafe? Save
the intended serum definition instead.

<details><summary>Solution 3</summary>


``` r
formula_concepts <- list(body = body_sets, systolic = omop_concept_set(sbp_id),
  diastolic = omop_concept_set(dbp_id), serum_creatinine = serum_set)
formula_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(formula_concepts, formula_file)
identical(readRDS(formula_file), formula_concepts)
```

```
#> [1] TRUE
```

Name matching is a discovery aid. The intended specimen, unit and source use
must all agree before formula execution.

</details>

## Collapse duplicate readings within a recorded day

An ordinary mean weights every reading. If the protocol gives each observed day
equal weight, reduce within person, concept, unit and recorded date first, then
reduce those daily values. Absent days are not filled.


``` r
daily_mean <- omop_number_daily(omop_number_rows(omop_event("measurement", body_sets$weight, unit = omop_unit(9529L))),
  reducer = omop_reduce("mean"), within_day = "mean")
daily_recipe <- omop_recipe(variables = list(weight = daily_mean))
daily_result <- recipe_execute(daily_recipe, out = "D_daily_weights", conns = conns)
knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_daily_weights$weight", datasources = conns)))
```



|Site |Statistic |     Value|
|:----|:---------|---------:|
|site |5%        |  7.757244|
|site |10%       |  9.730625|
|site |25%       | 35.703630|
|site |50%       | 75.000000|
|site |75%       | 80.890000|
|site |90%       | 86.648000|
|site |95%       | 90.504000|
|site |Mean      | 59.820033|

`within_day = "max"` asks a different question; `"first"` uses deterministic event
order. The outer reducer still controls how observed days contribute to the result.

**Exercise.** Compare a daily maximum followed by a mean.

<details><summary>Solution: change the within-day rule</summary>


``` r
daily_max <- omop_number_daily(omop_number_rows(omop_event("measurement", body_sets$weight, unit = omop_unit(9529L))),
  reducer = omop_reduce("mean"), within_day = "max")
daily_max_recipe <- omop_recipe(variables = list(weight = daily_max))
book_symbols(recipe_execute(daily_max_recipe, out = "D_daily_max_weights", conns = conns))
```

## Collapse repeated episodes deliberately

A person may have several eligible measurement episodes. Requesting person grain
requires an explicit collapse rule: first_episode, last_episode or any. This
collapses repeated population episodes, not duplicate source measurements.


``` r
episodes <- omop_population("weights", index = omop_index(weight_event, select = "all"))
collapsed <- omop_recipe(populations = list(episodes), variables = list(weight = weight),
  outputs = omop_output("people", rows = "weights", format = "wide", grain = "person",
    collapse = "first_episode"))
cat(grep("collapse|grain", recipe_explain(collapsed)$text, value = TRUE), sep = "\n")
```

```
#> Output 'people' [wide] rows 'weights', grain person (collapse first_episode)
#>   - output 'people': one row per person from an episode population, collapse = "first_episode"
```

``` r
book_symbols(recipe_execute(collapsed, out = c(people = "D_collapsed_weights"), conns = conns))
```

```
#>                people 
#> "D_collapsed_weights"
```

``` r
knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_collapsed_weights$weight", datasources = conns)))
```



|Site |Statistic |    Value|
|:----|:---------|--------:|
|site |5%        |  2.71000|
|site |10%       |  3.73000|
|site |25%       | 11.05000|
|site |50%       | 70.90000|
|site |75%       | 75.72500|
|site |90%       | 80.94000|

A same-day tolerance still does not average duplicate readings automatically.
Closest-value selection uses deterministic ordering; a mean weights eligible
rows. Document whether the problem is repeated episodes or duplicated source
records before choosing a collapse or reducer. The events chapter compares
record counts with distinct-day counts.

## Execute eGFR with declared synthetic inputs

The questionnaire helper can create synthetic standardized serum creatinine
measurements and explicitly named equation-sex categories. This is formula
practice, separate from the two clinical practice resources. Its partial birth
dates remain incomplete so that missing age still produces missing eGFR.


``` r
source("tools/book/fixture.R")
formula_practice <- book_fixture(formulas = TRUE, symbol = "book_formula")
formula_conns <- formula_practice$conns
formula_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Teaching standardized serum creatinine",
  domain = "Measurement", conns = formula_conns, symbol = "book_formula")$pooled
sex_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search(NULL, domain = "Gender", conns = formula_conns, symbol = "book_formula")$pooled
knitr::kable(rbind(formula_hits, sex_hits)[c("concept_name", "standard_concept", "vocabulary_id")])
```



|concept_name                           |standard_concept |vocabulary_id |
|:--------------------------------------|:----------------|:-------------|
|Teaching standardized serum creatinine |S                |Fixture       |
|FEMALE                                 |S                |Gender        |
|MALE                                   |S                |Gender        |

``` r
formula_id <- formula_hits$concept_id
formula_set <- omop_concept_set(formula_id)
knitr::kable(ds.omop.concept.locate(formula_id, scope = "pooled", conns = formula_conns, symbol = "book_formula")$pooled)
```



| concept_id|table_name  |concept_column         | n_records| n_persons|
|----------:|:-----------|:----------------------|---------:|---------:|
|     970001|measurement |measurement_concept_id |        20|        20|

``` r
knitr::kable(ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = formula_id,
  scope = "pooled", conns = formula_conns, symbol = "book_formula")$pooled)
```



|  n|concept_name            |value |
|--:|:-----------------------|:-----|
| 20|milligram per deciliter |8840  |

``` r
sex_ids <- setNames(sex_hits$concept_id, sex_hits$concept_name)
saveRDS(list(creatinine = formula_set, sex = sex_ids), formula_file)
```

These are local teaching concepts with no external mappings or ancestors.
The synthetic source explicitly defines standardized serum measurements in mg/dL.
The clinical equivalents would require assay and source validation.


``` r
serum_event <- omop_event("measurement", formula_set, unit = omop_unit(8840L))
creatinine <- omop_variable(event = serum_event,
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", missing = "keep"))
creatinine <- omop_number(creatinine, omop_number_spec(unit =
  omop_number_unit("unit:8840", "coordinate:idms_creatinine_mg_dl", factor = 1)))
egfr <- omop_formula_egfr_ckdepi2021(creatinine,
  age = omop_age_at(omop_anchor(serum_event, which = "first", scope = "episode")),
  sex = omop_variable(table = "person", column = "gender_concept_id"),
  sex_map = list(female = paste0("concept:", sex_ids[["FEMALE"]]),
    male = paste0("concept:", sex_ids[["MALE"]])))
egfr_recipe <- omop_recipe(
  populations = omop_population("measurements", index = omop_index(serum_event)),
  variables = list(egfr = egfr),
  outputs = omop_output("people", rows = "measurements", format = "wide"))
egfr_result <- recipe_execute(egfr_recipe, out = "D_egfr", conns = formula_conns, symbol = "book_formula")
knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_egfr$egfr", datasources = formula_conns)))
```



|Site |Statistic |     Value|
|:----|:---------|---------:|
|site |5%        |  34.11223|
|site |10%       |  34.11223|
|site |25%       |  45.57251|
|site |50%       |  98.00762|
|site |75%       | 114.93547|
|site |90%       | 117.24833|
|site |95%       | 117.24833|
|site |Mean      |  84.64730|

The output is an adult estimate in mL/min/1.73 m². Age is completed calendar years
at the selected creatinine measurement. Missing age or an unmapped equation-sex
category remains missing; the helper never guesses a branch or adds a race term.

**Exercise.** Inspect the formula provenance retained with the table.

<details><summary>Solution: retain the equation and its eligibility rules</summary>


``` r
formula_record <- recipe_codebook(egfr_result)[[1]]$formulas[[1]]
print(formula_record[c("id", "version", "equation", "unit", "eligibility")])
```

```
#> 
#> $unit
```

The formula definition version is separate from package version. Saving this
record makes the units, equation and adult eligibility explicit for a reviewer.

</details>

## Recap

Align meanings, units and dates before arithmetic. Native expressions preserve
private inputs and declared coordinates. BMI, MAP and ratios use named formula definitions; missing prerequisites are a reason to stop a formula study. Collapse
repeated episodes explicitly instead of letting duplicate rows change an analysis.

**Next:** [16. Longitudinal data: from events to analysis](book-16-longitudinal.html).
